Privacy notice

We collect as little as we can, use it only to run Compliance Clock, and never sell it.

Last updated: [date of launch]

Draft for legal review. This notice is a starting point written for a small UK business. Have it checked by a solicitor or data protection adviser before launch, and fill in the items marked [like this].

Who we are

Compliance Clock is run by Triple Bottom Line Ltd (company number [to add], registered office [to add]). We are the "controller" of your personal data. ICO registration number: [to add].

Contact us about privacy at [privacy email] or through our contact form.

What we collect and why

When you…We collectWhy, and our lawful basis
Sign up for the monthly emailEmail address; optionally your sector and company sizeTo send the email and tailor it to you. Consent, which you can withdraw any time with the unsubscribe link.
Use the contact formName, email, organisation (optional), your messageTo reply to you. Legitimate interests.
Buy a checklist or ProName, email, billing details (handled by our payment provider)To deliver what you bought and keep tax records. Contract and legal obligation.
Browse the siteAnonymous, aggregated visit statistics. No cookies, no personal profile.To understand which pages help people. Legitimate interests.

Cookies

We don't use advertising or tracking cookies, so you won't see a cookie banner. Our analytics tool [Plausible] works without cookies. If you choose light or dark mode, your browser remembers that choice in local storage on your own device. It never reaches us.

Who we share it with

We use a small number of trusted service providers ("processors") who handle data only on our instructions:

  • Website hosting: [Netlify]
  • Email delivery: [MailerLite or Buttondown]
  • Payments and digital delivery: [Lemon Squeezy or Paddle]. As "merchant of record" they are a separate controller for payment and tax data.
  • Analytics: [Plausible]

We never sell your data or share it with partners or sponsors. If a partner appears on our site and you contact them, that's between you and them.

Some providers may process data outside the UK. Where they do, we rely on UK adequacy regulations or the UK International Data Transfer Agreement or Addendum.

How long we keep it

  • Email subscribers: until you unsubscribe, then removed within 30 days (we keep a suppression record so we don't email you again).
  • Contact messages: up to 2 years, unless they relate to an ongoing matter.
  • Purchase records: 6 years, as required for tax.

Your rights

Under UK GDPR you can ask us to: see the data we hold about you; correct it; delete it; restrict or object to how we use it; and give you a copy to take elsewhere. Where we rely on consent, you can withdraw it at any time. We'll reply within one month.

If you're unhappy with how we've handled your data, please tell us first. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at ico.org.uk.

Changes to this notice

If we make significant changes, we'll update the date above and tell email subscribers.
